stem:
The diagram shows a bar magnet that Sahil cuts into three pieces. Each piece is labelled.

What should he expect about magnetic poles?

options.text: Each piece still has both a north pole and a south pole.
One piece is a lone north pole with no south pole.
Only the red-painted end on each piece is a magnetic pole.
The smallest piece has no poles at all.

teacher.key_rationale: North and south poles always exist in pairs. Cutting a magnet still gives smaller magnets with both poles. Paint colour does not create a lone pole, and even a small piece keeps paired poles.
teacher.figure_note: Rewrote source force block into three snapped magnet pieces, each labelled N and S.
